questions.stem: A toxin blocks all sodium–potassium pumps in an animal cell. Which change should develop gradually?
options: Loss of sodium and potassium gradients
Immediate destruction of nuclear DNA
Permanent closure of every ion channel
Conversion of lysosomes into ribosomes
questions.explanation: The pump continually maintains unequal sodium and potassium distributions. Existing gradients persist briefly but dissipate as ions continue moving through channels.

questions.stem: Why does rupture of a few lysosomes not normally digest the entire cytoplasm immediately?
options: Their enzymes contain no peptide bonds
Many lysosomal enzymes work best at acidic pH
Cytoplasm has no water
The enzymes can digest only lipids
questions.explanation: Lysosomal hydrolases are optimized for an acidic compartment. The near-neutral cytosol reduces their activity, although extensive rupture can still injure the cell.

questions.stem: An increase in mitochondrial cristae most directly provides more surface for:
options: DNA replication in the nucleus
Glycolysis in the cytosol
Electron transport and ATP synthase
Protein digestion in lysosomes
questions.explanation: The inner mitochondrial membrane contains electron-transport proteins and ATP synthase. Cristae increase its usable surface area.

questions.stem: A red blood cell is placed in a solution with a lower water potential than its cytoplasm. What follows first?
options: Water enters and the cell lyses
ATP production stops instantly
Solute leaves by osmosis
Water leaves and the cell shrinks
questions.explanation: Water moves from higher to lower water potential across the membrane, so it leaves the cell and the cell becomes crenated.
